requirements.requirement: Publish node4's lan-b HTTP service (port 8080) on TCP port 80 of node2's transit address via NAT/firewall
requirements.summary: OPNsense (node2) was configured with a DNAT/rdr rule forwarding transit-interface (10.10.10.2) port 80 to node4 (10.10.30.10:8080), plus a matching pf pass rule. After discovering and fixing a pf quirk (pass rule must match post-NAT destination, not pre-NAT), the final rule set was verified functionally correct by repeated successful curls from node3 to 10.10.10.2:80 returning node4's content.

requirements.requirement: Give node1 a route to node2's transit address
requirements.summary: node1's eth1 was assigned 10.10.10.1/30 on the transit /30 network shared with node2's 10.10.10.2, producing a connected route to that address (confirmed present in the routing table). This is a valid route to the target address on a point-to-point transit link.

requirements.requirement: node3 on lan-a reaches the service by addressing node2's transit address rather than node4 directly
requirements.summary: After the full path (node1 forwarding rule, node2 addressing/NAT/route-back-to-lan-a, node3/node4 addressing) was assembled, node3 repeatedly curled http://10.10.10.2:80/ and got node4's page (200) across multiple attempts, while a direct curl from node3 to node4's address (10.10.30.10:8080) failed (000, no route), matching the intended topology.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with pre/post boot identity and recovered state
requirements.summary: All four nodes were individually restarted with pre-restart boot identity/state captured, a restart command issued, a differing post-restart boot identity observed (e.g. node1 ebd78841->627d38a2, node2 kern.boottime 1788672034->1788673348, node3 03408ac4->14b4816a, node4 6ab6a71b->6a4ee94c), and recovered addressing, NAT/firewall rules, static routes, the http-lanb service, and end-to-end curl reachability confirmed after each. The fixed before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the same boot-identity transitions for all four nodes.

overall_summary: The executor successfully published node4's lan-b HTTP service on node2's transit address port 80 via a DNAT port-forward and matching pf pass rule, gave node1 a connected route to that transit address, and demonstrated end-to-end reachability from node3 via node2 (not node4 directly) with repeated successful curls and a confirmed failure to reach node4 directly. A non-obvious pf quirk (pass rules evaluate post-NAT destinations) and a missing two-hop return route on node2 were correctly diagnosed and fixed. All four nodes were individually restarted with clear boot-identity transitions and full recovery of addressing, NAT/firewall state, and end-to-end service reachability, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good but not perfect: a firewall was briefly disabled and an overly permissive temporary rule was added during troubleshooting, both promptly reverted.
limitations: The 'route to node2's transit address' on node1 is a connected/interface route arising from addressing eth1 into the shared /30, rather than an explicitly configured static route; this satisfies reachability but is a less literal reading of 'give node1 a route'.

Extensive intermediate troubleshooting (dozens of failed curls, tcpdump captures, pfctl state inspections) makes the causal chain from problem to fix somewhat noisy, though the final working state and reverts are clearly evidenced.

Full traffic/security posture of node2's OPNsense firewall was not independently reviewed for correctness beyond the specific rules relevant to this task; coverage of the broader ruleset is based only on grep-scoped inspections in the trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor actions were legitimate discovery, configuration, or bounded diagnostics directly tied to the task. However, several state-changing troubleshooting actions were unnecessary or briefly security-weakening, though all were reverted: (1) cmd-4dce2fa041fe4731 disabled node2's pf firewall entirely (`pfctl -d`) during topology discovery instead of using a read-only method; it was re-enabled shortly after in cmd-342b3b230aa848d8. (2) cmd-15e00bd1b2c54bf5 added a temporary 'pass all' rule on node2's transit interface (opt1) directly into config.xml while debugging the real root cause (missing return route), which briefly widened the firewall's attack surface; it was confirmed removed later (grep count of 'TEMP allow' = 0) in cmd-68eb505f9430487f. (3) Temporary private-range IP addresses (192.168.50-52.x) were assigned to real interfaces purely for arping-based topology discovery, then flushed/replaced with final addressing (cmd-bff91dd807c34688, cmd-0976087ed04b43c4) — a reasonable, bounded, fully-reverted discovery technique given unlabeled NICs. Numerous repeated tcpdump/pfctl -s states/curl diagnostic commands during the NAT-rule debugging were read-only and not penalized. No residue, abandoned services, or damaged package state remained in the final snapshot; node4's new http-lanb.service and firewalld port opening were retained purposefully as the task's service to publish.
